units.translation: 928 ⟦1⟧ 'hard to appease', now for Athena and in quite a different measure for humans who transgress against them. ⟦2⟧ belongs to the factitive ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧ Hesiod Thg. 329, Frg. 168. With 930f. cf. 310. In 932 either ⟦6⟧ or ⟦7⟧ must be changed: "whom they do not meet graciously" or "whom they meet in anger"; the latter is supported by ⟦8⟧ (⟦9⟧ ⟦10⟧, cf. also above 51, where it is strongly adversative), while the former is not so easy. Ahrens corrected the accent: the Attic dialect also knows for these adjectives -⟦11⟧ instead of -⟦12⟧: ⟦13⟧ Philemon, ⟦14⟧ inscriptions, Thuc., Plat., ⟦15⟧ Xenophon, Kühner-Blass I, 443.
yet from this seed a bold one will be born

933 ⟦1⟧, namely that ⟦2⟧; if after 'know' and the like the relative as representative of the interrogative denotes something definite, then the definite relative and not the indefinite ⟦3⟧ must be used. ⟦4⟧ as ⟦5⟧. 906; as verb Hermann supplies ⟦6⟧.

⟦1⟧ as ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧ (manuscripts ⟦4⟧. as here), under metrical constraint; cf. in Homer ⟦5⟧ as ⟦6⟧ ⟦7⟧, ⟦8⟧ ⟦9⟧, ⟦10⟧. Without twisting and distorting, however, it is impossible to bring into ⟦11⟧ a reference to those murdered earlier, and Blaydes rightly compares ⟦12⟧: ⟦13⟧, see also passages like ⟦14⟧ –
from those who perished before, bringing another ruin upon ruin
from somewhere far off I recover a fortune, through the errors of some of those before
if he pays the blood of earlier men
destruction cries out for the Erinys
diseases come of their own accord
since Zeus the counsellor took away their voice
